newsitem.title: UK: Prince Charles heads for Hong Kong handover.
newsitem.headline: Prince Charles heads for Hong Kong handover.

text.p: Britain's heir to the throne Prince Charles flew from London on Friday bound for Hong Kong, where he will attend ceremonies marking the British colony's handover to China on June 30.
The prince left London's Heathrow airport aboard a chartered British Airways 747 jet which carried 200 members of the British delegation to the ceremony.
Among those travelling with the prince were Foreign Secretary Robin Cook, former prime minister Edward Heath and former foreign secretary Lord (Geoffrey) Howe.

The prince, representing his mother, head of state Queen Elizabeth, will hand back the territory to Chinese President Jiang Zemin. He will then sail home on the royal yacht Britannia with governor Chris Patten.
